school: 马其顿国王/锤砧战术与远程远征的开创者/希腊化时代的奠基人
historical_significance: 亚历山大大帝（前356—前323），马其顿国王腓力二世之子，亚里士多德的弟子。前336年即位后，两年内平定希腊与色雷斯叛乱，摧毁底比斯。前334年率马其顿联军渡赫勒斯滂东征波斯，格拉尼库斯河首战破敌；前333年伊苏斯会战击溃大流士三世亲率大军；前332年经围困夺提尔与加沙，入埃及被奉为法老，建亚历山大城；前331年高加米拉会战以斜击与骑兵锥形突击彻底摧毁波斯主力，焚波斯波利斯；此后经里海东岸、巴克特里亚、索格狄亚那追击篡位者贝苏斯，前327年越兴都库什山入印度，前326年海达斯佩斯河会战以包抄与雨夜奇袭战胜波鲁斯王，因部众拒进而止步印度河，前323年病逝巴比伦，年三十三。他一生未尝败绩，以马其顿方阵为'砧'、伙伴骑兵为'锤'的诸兵种协同与斜线突击，把会战艺术推到古代顶峰；以建城约二十座的'亚历山大城'网络、波斯精英收编与东西通婚推动希腊化时代开启，使希腊语言、货币与思想由此后三百年浸润从地中海到阿富汗的广大世界。
historical_significance_en: Alexander the Great (356-323 BCE), son of Philip II of Macedon and pupil of Aristotle, acceded in 336 BCE and within two years crushed revolts in Greece and Thrace, razing Thebes. In 334 BCE he led the Macedonian league across the Hellespont against Persia, winning the Granicus; shattered Darius III's host at Issus in 333; took Tyre and Gaza by siege, entered Egypt and was acclaimed pharaoh while founding Alexandria in 332; and at Gaugamela in 331 annihilated the Persian main force with an oblique advance and wedge cavalry charge, burning Persepolis. He then pursued the usurper Bessus through the Caspian coast, Bactria and Sogdiana, crossed the Hindu Kush in 327 into India, defeated Porus at the Hydaspes in 326 by envelopment and a night river crossing, and turned back only when his army refused to go on. He died at Babylon in 323 BCE, aged thirty-three, undefeated in battle. His combined-arms art—phalanx as anvil, Companion cavalry as hammer, delivered obliquely—set the ancient summit of battle craft; his network of some twenty 'Alexandrias', his incorporation of Persian elites, and his mass weddings opened the Hellenistic age, steeping the world from the Mediterranean to Afghanistan in Greek language, coinage, and thought for the three centuries that followed.

cross_references.relation_type: 歼灭战艺术的东西双璧：斜击与迂回
cross_references.description_zh: 亚历山大与韩信相隔两个世纪，同为'以会战灭国'的大师：前者以方阵牵制、骑兵斜击直取敌军统帅中枢（高加米拉），后者以背水列阵、奇兵迂回夺敌纵深（井陉之战）。二人共同说明：歼灭战的本质不是兵力比拼，而是把敌人的指挥中枢与退路同时变成死地——一个从正面打掉头脑，一个从侧后切断脊柱。
cross_references.description_en: Alexander and Han Xin, two centuries apart, were twin masters of the war of annihilation by decisive battle: the former pinned the enemy line with his phalanx while his cavalry struck obliquely at the enemy commander's center (Gaugamela); the latter held a riverline with his back to the water while flying columns took the enemy's depth (Jingxing). Together they show that annihilation is not a contest of numbers but of making the enemy's command brain and line of retreat both lethal ground—one striking the head from the front, the other severing the spine from flank and rear.

cross_references.relation_type: 机动力崇拜的师承：从伙伴骑兵到军团建制
cross_references.description_zh: 拿破仑毕生研读亚历山大战史，把'集中优势兵力于决定点、以机动制造以多打少'推到火器时代：亚历山大用骑兵锤砧，拿破仑用军团体系与炮兵集中。二人同样以个人魅力在前线示范，同样以合法性包装（罗马加冕/埃及法老衔）统合多元帝国，也同样止步于超越补给的远征极限——俄国的冬天与印度河的部众哗变，是同一条后勤铁律的两次判决。
cross_references.description_en: Napoleon read Alexander all his life, translating the hammer-anvil of the Companions into the corps system and massed artillery of the gunpowder age: concentrating force at the decisive point to create local superiority by maneuver. Both led from the front on personal charisma, both wrapped multi-ethnic empires in legitimacy (imperial coronation; the pharaoh's titles), and both met the same logistical iron law at the far edge of overextension—the Russian winter and the mutiny at the Hydaspes as two verdicts of one rule.
